kind: Eighteen runs on the server's GPU: the loop of practice_with_rehearsal.json (capped practice from rewarded attempts, with the written chains of 1 to 4 hops rehearsed in every round) with its cap at 8, at 12 and at 16 hops, from the stack and from the Transformer, with seeds 0, 1 and 2 each. The runs with the cap at 8 are the seeds that practice_with_rehearsal.json registered as what follows a pass; the runs with the cap at 12 and 16 are the next step it names, registered here before they start.
why: Two questions. First, whether rehearsal holds the chains that practice wins with other seeds than the one that showed it. Second, what the cap is still needed for. The cap stood at 8 hops because a guess pays more the longer the chain: a line holds 24 assignments whatever its hops, so a long chain leaves few other digits, and a guess among the digits that a name points to is right 0.23 of the time at 8 hops, 0.24 at 9, 0.28 at 12, 0.37 at 16 and 0.55 at 20 (experiments/hop_tasks.py floors, 4,000 lines a length). The staircase steps down when fewer than a quarter of a round's attempts are rewarded: up to 9 hops a model that had lost its chains and guessed would be sent back to shorter tasks; from 10 hops on a guess pays a quarter or more. With the cap at 12 or 16 that brake is gone, and what holds the chains is the rehearsal and the chains' own higher pay. The uncapped loop without rehearsal lost them (practice_written_chains.json: the staircase climbed to 23 hops, where the guess pays). Under the cap at 8 the stack already writes chains it never practised: its model kept at round 700 of practice_within_reach.json's cap-bursts-stack wrote the whole chain right in 0.815 of the answers at 12 hops, 0.720 at 16 and 0.335 at 20. Whether practising those lengths takes the chains further, and whether the loop still holds, is not known.
loop: experiments/practice_loop.py as practice_with_rehearsal.json ran it: every round 16 tasks at the current number of hops, verified, 8 attempts each at temperature 1.0 with room for 64 bytes (a written chain of 8 hops takes 23 bytes, of 12 hops 35, of 16 hops 47, of 20 hops 59); reward 1 if the last byte before the newline is the answer; the staircase from 4 hops, capped (--longest-hops); only attempts above their task's mean teach (--dips 0); every round rehearses the written chains of 16 fresh tasks of 1, 2, 3 or 4 hops with weight 1 (--rehearse 16); Adam at 3e-5, gradients clipped at 1; 2,000 rounds.

arms.r8-stack-s0, r8-stack-s1, r8-stack-s2: --longest-hops 8 --dips 0 --rehearse 16 --evaluate-hops 2 4 6 8 12 16 --seed 0, 1, 2, from chain-stack (the averaged weights of written_chains.json)
arms.r8-tf-s0 ... r16-tf-s2: the same nine runs from chain-tf
arms.beside them: rehearse-bursts-stack and rehearse-bursts-tf of practice_with_rehearsal.json: the cap at 8 with seed 0 on the laptop's GPU, read in their own record

code: Commit ef30a84 (the server's copy v18p): the practice loop of 38c215f with two of the trainer's speed switches. The stack's runs take --exact-products --fused-reads; the Transformer has neither whole-number products nor reads, and its runs take no switch. All 18 runs side by side on one GPU of the server (CUDA, through MPS) in the night window of 2026-11-27, which closes at 06:15 UTC; a run that the window's end cuts short starts afresh in the next window with the same seed (a run does not go on from its middle) and is the registered run. Checked before recording: on a CPU this copy repeats the frozen copy that runs practice_with_rehearsal.json round for round (5 rounds with rehearsal from chain-stack, seed 99: the two logs equal byte for byte). On the server's GPU its evaluation of both models before practice repeats the laptop's at 2, 4, 6, 8 and 12 hops in every number (accuracy, whole chain, mean bytes), for the stack by each way (as it is, with exact products, with fused reads beside them); on the server's CPU the stack's answers at 6 hops take 19.21 bytes in the mean for 18.96 and every other number is the same. On the GPU 60 rounds with seed 99 gave the same log byte for byte by each of the three ways. A run on this GPU does not repeat itself to the bit: two runs of 30 rounds from chain-stack as they are gave the same log and weights that differ in the input synapses alone (by up to 3e-8, in 0.04% of the entries), the run with both switches differs from them by no more than that, and two runs from chain-tf gave the same log and differ in every tensor by up to 6e-8. A run on another device, or with fused reads, is another run as another seed is: seed 0 here is not the laptop's arm again. Speed, 60 rounds from chain-stack beside one other job on the GPU: 0.72 s a round as it is, 0.68 with exact products, 0.65 with fused reads beside them; the Transformer 0.16 s; the laptop's GPU takes about 1.1 s a round for the stack.
measure: As practice_with_rehearsal.json. Along the way: before the first round and after every 100 rounds, 200 tasks each of 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16 hops answered greedily (--evaluate-every 100 --evaluate-hops 2 4 6 8 12 16 --evaluate-tasks 200), each scored model kept; these tasks are drawn from the run's seed, so every seed is scored on its own tasks along the way. After the last round, the same for every run: --evaluate 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 10 12 16 20 --evaluate-tasks 200 --max-bytes 64 --seed 0 (the tasks of the earlier screens): the accuracy of the last byte with its 95% Wilson interval, the share of answers that write the whole chain right with its interval, the mean bytes. The rounds' log with the staircase and the rehearsal's loss.
reading: Every run is read by the marks of practice_with_rehearsal.json: on its evaluation after 2,000 rounds (a) at 6 hops an accuracy of at least 0.50 with at least half of the answers writing the whole chain right, (b) the same at 8 hops, (c) a mean accuracy over 1 to 4 hops of at least 0.95; and (h) at every one of its 20 evaluations from round 100 to round 2,000 it meets (b) and answers at least 0.95 of the tasks of 2 hops and of 4 hops. A run holds if it meets all four. (1) Seeds: rehearsal keeps what practice wins if the stack's three runs with the cap at 8 all hold. If one does not, it holds with some seeds and not with others: no pass, and the lost run's rounds are read before anything is built on the loop. (2) The cap raised, for the stack. (2a) The loop still holds without the staircase's brake if the three runs with the cap at 16 all hold; the same is read for the cap at 12. (2b) A raised cap takes the chains further if, in at least two of the three seeds, the share of answers that write the whole chain right at 16 hops, or that share at 20 hops, is at least 0.10 higher in the run with the cap at 16 than in the run with the cap at 8 and the same seed, with the two 95% intervals apart, and in no seed the run with the cap at 8 is ahead by that margin at either length. The whole chain is read and not the accuracy, because at these lengths a guess is right in 0.37 and 0.55 of the tasks. A seed whose run with the cap at 8 writes 0.90 or more of the 16-hop chains has no room at 16 hops and is read at 20 alone. The runs with the cap at 12 are reported by the same shares as the step between. (3) The stack against the Transformer under each cap, as before: one practises further if at 6 hops and at 8 its accuracy after 2,000 rounds is at least 0.10 above the other's with the two 95% intervals apart, read for each seed; it stands for a cap if it holds in at least two of the three seeds and the other model is ahead in none. Reported and not read: the accuracies and whole-chain shares at 10, 12, 16 and 20 hops of every run, the evaluations along the way at 12 and 16 hops, the share of rounds the staircase spent at its cap and the rounds at which it left it, the rounds' solve rates and whole-chain shares, the rehearsal's loss, the mean bytes. Synthetic tasks of one family: whether the practice loop holds and how far it reaches, not a claim about reasoning in language. What follows: if (1) passes, this loop is the practice of the one-model plan, as registered. If (2a) and (2b) pass with the cap at 16, the cap is no part of the loop's safety for this family, and the next registration puts a second family of tasks into the same loop. If a run with a raised cap loses its chains, the cap stays at 8, where a model that guesses is sent back to shorter tasks, and the next registration tries a reward that asks for more than the answer before longer chains are practised.
seen_before_recording: The laptop's arm (rehearse-bursts-stack, seed 0) had finished when this was recorded and meets (a), (b), (c) and (h), so the follow-up that practice_with_rehearsal.json registered is due; its result is appended to that file after this record. It met (h) at every one of its 20 evaluations: at 8 hops an accuracy of 0.955 to 1.000 with the whole chain right in 0.935 to 0.990 of the answers, at 12 hops 0.745 to 0.980 (0.660 to 0.975). After 2,000 rounds, accuracy (whole chain): 6 hops 0.995 (0.995), 8 hops 0.990 (0.985), 10 hops 0.995 (0.980), 12 hops 0.980 (0.975), 16 hops 0.905 (0.875), 20 hops 0.430 (0.345); mean accuracy over 1 to 4 hops 0.9988. The uncapped and capped runs without rehearsal are recorded in practice_written_chains.json and practice_within_reach.json (five of the latter's six arms were not finished at this time). No run of this record had started.
